construction_markdown: No leaderboard construction is submitted. I analyze the standard product-distance concatenation with a binary linear inner code `[8192,m,d]_2` and a fixed-length generalized Reed–Solomon outer code `[131072,K,131073-K]_{2^m}`. Two exact parity-extension Delsarte cubics force every target-feasible instance to have `m=17`, `d=4088`, and `K=1`. Hence this entire architecture has binary dimension at most `17`, below the verified `RM(1,30)` baseline `31` and the shared dimension-1040 candidate.

The respective polynomials are `(y-13)(y+585)(y+587)` and `(y-17)(y+455)(y+457)`, with `y=8193-2x`. Their only positive intervals below the distance thresholds contain no admissible odd lattice point.

distance_audit: The immutable target factors exactly as `535822336=4088*131072`.
Parity extension maps every pair originally at distance `x` to distance `x+(x mod 2)`; hence distance `>=4089` becomes `>=4090`, while distance `>=4088` remains `>=4088`.
Both cubic certificates apply to every pairwise distance through the Delsarte character-square identity, rather than only to generator rows or selected words.

A nonzero outer RS word has at least `131073-K` nonzero symbols, and every such symbol contributes an inner block of weight at least `d`; therefore every nonzero concatenated word has weight at least `d(131073-K)`.
Once `d<=4088`, any `K>=2` gives product distance at most `4088*131071=535818248`, which is `4088` below target.
For an ordinary tensor product with both factor dimensions at least two, relative distance is at most `(2/3)^2=4/9<511/1024`; thus it cannot meet the target.
explicitness_audit: Both Delsarte polynomials, all Krawtchouk coefficients, evaluations, quotients, and remainders are displayed as exact integers.
Parity extension is the symbolic map `c -> (c,wt(c) mod 2)`; no finite choice is hidden.
The RS obstruction explicitly assumes a binary-linear inner alphabet embedding, `131072` distinct outer evaluation positions, and the ordinary product-distance certificate.
No random sampling, numerical construction search, unavailable constituent, padding, or hidden asymptotic constant is used.

obstructions: The standard product-certified inner-8192/outer-131072 RS architecture has binary dimension at most 17 and therefore cannot beat the verified dimension-31 baseline.
No binary code of length 8193, distance at least 4090, and cardinality `2^17` exists.
No binary code of length 8193, distance at least 4088, and cardinality `2^18` exists.
A nontrivial tensor product of two binary codes cannot attain relative distance `511/1024`.
A Plotkin transform `(u,u+v)` at this length can add at most one binary dimension through its `v` constituent.
These conclusions do not bound arbitrary binary linear codes, symbol-sensitive concatenations, or other inner/outer length factorizations.

proof_markdown:
# Parity-extension obstruction for the `8192 × 131072` RS product route

Set `T=535822336`.

## 1. Finite Delsarte lemma

For a binary code `X` of length `n` and size `M`, define its normalized distance distribution

`A_i=M^(-1)|{(u,v) in X^2 : d(u,v)=i}|`.

Thus `A_0=1` and `sum_i A_i=M`. For the binary Krawtchouk polynomial `K_j`, character orthogonality gives

`sum_i A_i K_j(i)=M^(-1) sum_{|S|=j} |sum_{u in X} (-1)^(sum_{r in S}u_r)|^2 >=0`.

Consequently, if `F=sum_j f_jK_j` has `f_0>0`, all `f_j>=0`, and `F(i)<=0` at every possible nonzero distance `i>=d`, then

`f_0M <= sum_i A_iF(i) <=F(0)`.

Hence `M<=F(0)/f_0`. This argument applies even to nonlinear codes.

## 2. Two odd-lattice cubic certificates

Take `n=8193` and put `y=n-2x`. Then every integral distance gives an odd integer `y`. The first three Krawtchouk polynomials satisfy

`K_1=y`, `K_2=(y^2-8193)/2`, and `K_3=(y^3-24577y)/6`.

For distance `4090`, define

`F_1(x)=(y-13)(y+585)(y+587)`.

For `x>=4090`, one has odd `y<=13`. The only interval below 13 on which this cubic is positive is `(-587,-585)`, which contains no odd integer. Thus `F_1(x)<=0` at every allowed distance. Direct expansion gives

`F_1=5031552K_0+352736K_1+2318K_2+6K_3`.

All coefficients are positive, and

`F_1(0)=8180*8778*8780=630439471200`

`=5031552*125297+1100256`.

Therefore

`A_2(8193,4090)<=125297<131072=2^17`.  (1)

For distance `4088`, define

`F_2(x)=(y-17)(y+455)(y+457)`.

Here the only positive interval below 17 is `(-457,-455)`, again containing no odd integer. Its exact expansion is

`F_2=3797840K_0+217008K_1+1790K_2+6K_3`,

and

`F_2(0)=8176*8648*8650=611607315200`

`=3797840*161040+3161600`.

Thus

`A_2(8193,4088)<=161040<262144=2^18`.  (2)

## 3. Parity extension

For a binary word `c`, set

`E(c)=(c, wt(c) mod 2)`.

This map is binary linear on a linear code and preserves dimension. A pair originally at distance `x` becomes a pair at distance `x+(x mod 2)`. Therefore:

- a code of distance at least `4089` extends to distance at least `4090`;
- a code of distance at least `4088` extends to distance at least `4088`.

By (1), any binary linear `[8192,m,>=4089]` code has `2^m<=125297`, hence `m<=16`. By (2), any `[8192,m,>=4088]` code has `2^m<=161040`, hence `m<=17`.

## 4. Concatenation consequence

Let `B` be a binary linear `[8192,m,d]_2` inner code, identify `F_{2^m}` binary-linearly with `B`, and let the outer code be a generalized Reed–Solomon code

`R=[131072,K,131073-K]_{2^m}`.

Having 131072 distinct evaluation points requires `m>=17`. Coordinatewise inner encoding is binary linear and injective, so the concatenation has exact length

`8192*131072=2^30`

and binary dimension `mK`. Every nonzero outer word has at least `131073-K` nonzero symbols, so every nonzero concatenated word has weight at least

`d(131073-K)`.

Suppose this product certificate reaches `T`. Since `131073-K<=131072`,

`d>=ceil(T/131072)=4088`.

The second parity-extension bound gives `m<=17`; field feasibility therefore forces `m=17`. The first bound rules out `d>=4089` at dimension 17, so `d<=4088`. Hence `d=4088`. Because

`T=4088*131072`,

the product inequality now forces `131073-K=131072`, namely `K=1`. Thus every feasible code in this architecture has

`dim=17*1=17`.

This is strictly below the verified RM dimension 31.

## 5. Other elementary product transformations

For every binary linear `[L,k,d]` code,

`(2^k-1)d <= L*2^(k-1)`,

because each active coordinate is one on exactly half the codewords. If `k>=2`, then `d/L<=2/3`. The tensor product of two nontrivial binary linear codes has relative distance equal to the product of the factor relative distances, hence at most `4/9<511/1024`; it cannot reach the campaign target.

For the Plotkin transform `{(u,u+v):u in U,v in V}` of two length-`2^29` codes, the distance is exactly `min(2d(U),d(V))`. Meeting the target requires `d(V)/2^29>=511/512>2/3`, so the same average-weight lemma forces `dim(V)<=1`. Thus this transformation can add at most one dimension.

proof_steps.proof: The Krawtchouk transform of the normalized distance distribution is an explicit sum of squared binary character sums. Nonnegative Krawtchouk coefficients and nonpositive off-diagonal values give `M<=F(0)/f_0`.
proof_steps.statement: The finite Delsarte polynomial bound holds for every binary code.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed cubic is nonpositive on every admissible odd `y<=13`, has Krawtchouk coefficients `(5031552,352736,2318,6)`, and has exact quotient `125297+1100256/5031552`.
The displayed cubic is nonpositive on every admissible odd `y<=17`, has coefficients `(3797840,217008,1790,6)`, and has exact quotient `161040+3161600/3797840`.
The map `c -> (c,wt(c) mod 2)` preserves cardinality and linear dimension and changes every pair distance `x` to `x+(x mod 2)`.
The outer-to-inner map is binary linear and injective. Lengths multiply, binary dimension is `mK`, and each nonzero outer symbol contributes an inner block of weight at least `d`.

Field size gives `m>=17`; the second cubic gives `m<=17`. Product distance gives `d>=4088`; the first cubic gives `d<=4088`. Exact factorization of the target then forces outer distance 131072 and `K=1`.
proof_steps.statement: Every target-feasible code in the standard `8192 × 131072` RS product-distance class has dimension at most 17.

proof_steps.proof: Average weight gives relative distance at most `2/3` for each factor of dimension at least two, while tensor relative distances multiply.
proof_steps.statement: A tensor product of two nontrivial binary linear factors cannot attain relative distance `511/1024`.

proof_steps.proof: The transform distance is `min(2d(U),d(V))`; its second constituent would need relative distance `511/512`, forcing dimension at most one by average weight.
proof_steps.statement: A standard Plotkin lift can add at most one dimension at the target.

theorem_statement: Let `B` be a binary linear `[8192,m,d]_2` code and let `R` be a generalized Reed–Solomon `[131072,K,131073-K]_{2^m}` code on distinct evaluation points. If the ordinary concatenation product certificate satisfies `d(131073-K)>=535822336`, then necessarily `m=17`, `d=4088`, and `K=1`; consequently the binary concatenation has dimension `mK=17`. Thus this entire product-distance architecture cannot beat the verified dimension-31 baseline.
